title: Persistency Share of the Universal Life Insurance Overloan Protection Charge
content:
The share of the overloan protection charge an Ashgrove Universal Life Insurance policy pays follows the number of premium payments in the policy's activity history, each premium received entry counting as one payment.

## Schedule

| Premium payments in the activity history | Share of the overloan protection charge paid |
|---|---|
| **15** or more (the long-persistency number) | Long persistency share, **90%** (0.90) |
| **10** to 14 (at least the mid-persistency number, fewer than 15) | Mid persistency share, **95%** (0.95) |
| Fewer than 10 | The whole charge |

The share multiplies the charge: a policy paying the 90% share pays nine tenths of the charge it would otherwise pay, before the charge is rounded to the cent.

## Boundary cases (hypothetical)

| Premium payments | Share |
|---|---|
| 9 | Whole charge |
| 10 | 95% |
| 14 | 95% |
| 15 | 90% |
| 40 | 90% |

## Points of judgement

- The count is the number of premium payments: forty monthly payments count forty times, one single payment once.
- A charge of $7000.0000 before the share becomes $6650.0000 at 95% and $6300.0000 at 90% (hypothetical figures).
